notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 03/12/2026
Patient: Kazuko Howe, 83-year-old female

Reason for Study:
Evaluation of suspected sleep-disordered breathing.

Study Details:
Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 03/12/2026.

Findings:
The study revealed multiple respiratory events during sleep. Central and mixed apneas comprised 13% of all events. Oxygen saturation remained stable with occasional mild desaturations.

Sleep Architecture:
Sleep stages were appropriately distributed with normal REM and non-REM cycles. No significant abnormalities in sleep continuity were observed.

Conclusion:
The polysomnography indicates the presence of central and mixed apneas contributing to sleep disruption. Further clinical correlation and management are recommended.

Signed,
Sleep Medicine Physician

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/11/2026
Patient: Kazuko Howe, 83-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Ms. Howe has a history of sleep-related breathing issues. She has been using CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 27.8 kg/m2.

Assessment:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.1 hours per night on 43% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options for sleep-disordered breathing including positional therapy and oral appliance therapy. Continue to monitor symptoms and reassess as needed. Provide education and support for adherence to alternative therapies.

Follow-up:
Schedule follow-up appointment in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise.
